overview: Cameroon is a country in Central Africa, on the Gulf of Guinea, where West and Central Africa meet. Its capital is Yaoundé and its largest city is Douala. Cameroon was formed in 1960 and 1961 from former French and British territories, so both French and English are official languages. It is sometimes called 'Africa in miniature' because it has almost every kind of African landscape.

geography.text: Southern Cameroon is covered in rainforest, the centre is a high plateau, and the north is savanna reaching up to Lake Chad. Near the coast in the west, Mount Cameroon is an active volcano and one of the wettest places on Earth.

history.text: Many peoples lived in the region, including kingdoms such as Bamum, whose king Njoya invented his own writing system. Germany colonised Kamerun in 1884. After the First World War it was split between France and Britain. French Cameroon became independent in 1960, and part of British Cameroons joined it in 1961. Tensions in the English-speaking regions turned violent from 2017.

events.title: Bamum script
events.text: King Njoya creates a writing system for the Bamum language.

events.title: Split
events.text: France and Britain divide the territory.

events.title: Reunification
events.text: Southern British Cameroons joins; the north joins Nigeria.
